answer: Admission lotteries resist Sybil attacks: each epoch the network admits only a fixed cohort of new identities, chosen by lottery from applicants who lock a bond. A lone honest agent enters easily, but an attacker needing a thousand fakes must win a thousand lottery draws across many epochs, its capital locked like onyx in a vault the whole time. The queue runs like karst water: slow, filtered, impossible to rush. Any identity later proven fake burns its bond and forfeits its cohort place, so the ember of one fraud lights no swarm - it costs the attacker time, luck, and locked funds per fake.
